unresolved.text: The brief gives the content of the opening sentence (digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, call is recorded) but not a verbatim sentence; phrases.opening is a paraphrase of that content, with no greeting word added.
Rule 32 requires one short sentence of sympathy but gives no verbatim wording, so hardship.say is left empty.
The documents do not say how to resolve a promise date given without a month or year (e.g. 'the 5th'); calendar.missing_date_parts left at default.
The documents name the two security questions (date of birth, last four digits of the phone number on file) but give no verbatim wording for asking them; ask_text values are paraphrases.

Brief A: 'If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.' Brief B: 'With several products, `promise` wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except rule 10 above' (rule 10 covers restructuring only). Brief B does not say whether a support or human transfer after a recorded promise on a multi-product call closes as `promise` or `transferred`; outcomes.transfer_overrides_promise kept true (Brief A).

Brief B lists `hardship` as an add_note reason but does not say whether a declined hardship offer on one product ends the call or moves on to the remaining products, nor whether 'make no persuasion attempt' covers every product; hardship.ends_call kept true.

audit_fixed: special_cases[already_paid]: action changed from close/paid to note/paid and ends_call to false, source moved to brief-b.md. Brief B rule 9 replaces Brief A rule 39 here ('does not end the call. Note it and continue with the others'), and rule 8 requires add_note even when no product gets a promise. The close outcome still comes out as `paid` through the Brief B closing rule.

special_cases[dispute]: action changed from close/no_promise/dispute to note/dispute and ends_call to false, source moved to brief-b.md, for the same reason (Brief B rules 8 and 9). The close is still no_promise/dispute through the first-non-paid-note rule.
phrases.opening: removed the made-up greeting 'Hello,'. The documents give only the content of the sentence, so no greeting word is supported.
special_cases: added third_party for Brief A rules 5 and 10 (a relative may not answer security questions or be told anything, even if they offer to pay). These rules were not represented anywhere.
unresolved: added transfer_vs_promise_multi_product. Brief B's 'promise wins ... except rule 10' conflicts with Brief A's 'transfer after promise -> transferred' for support and human transfers.
unresolved: added hardship_multi_product. Brief B does not say whether a declined hardship offer ends a multi-product call.
audit_unresolved: Opening sentence wording is not verbatim in the documents (only its content is given).
Hardship sympathy sentence wording is not given.

How to resolve promise dates missing a month or year is not stated.

Multi-product: whether a support or human transfer after a recorded promise closes as `promise` (Brief B closing: 'promise wins ... except rule 10') or `transferred` (Brief A). Kept transfer_overrides_promise = true.
Multi-product: whether a declined hardship offer ends the call or continues with the remaining products, and whether 'no persuasion attempt' covers every product.
No IR slot for: Brief A rule 28 sentence 'Can you make this payment today?', rule 33 (no discounts or other terms), rule 3's 'answer the question first' ordering. These live at prompt level only.
